lifecycle.creation_reason: Commit b1802e5d, an earlier microtask in this same work packet, reworked the knowledge_* API modules and the flight recorder emitter and dropped accessors that other microtasks' tests assert through. Seven backend test targets cannot compile as a result, and two of them carry the acceptance proofs for MT-108 and MT-105. The MT-141 implementer found this, refused to delete the tests to reach a green compile, and stopped at BLOCKED_ON_DEPENDENCY. This microtask restores what was dropped.
lifecycle.why_a_separate_microtask: MT-141's forbidden_paths exclude src/backend/handshake_core/src/**. The repair is product code, not test code. MT-141 was right not to reach for it.
lifecycle.urgency: This is the gate on the largest remaining microtask in the packet. MT-141 cannot compile its last 7 targets, cannot run its suite, and cannot satisfy AC-141-4 or PT-141-2 until this lands.

takeover_2026_09_06.authority: Operator explicitly requested takeover and completion to READY_FOR_VALIDATION

scope.summary: Restore the accessors and visibility that commit b1802e5d removed from src/backend/handshake_core/src/**, so the seven remaining backend test targets compile and MT-108's and MT-105's acceptance proofs are executable again. The durable data and behaviour still exist; only the ways of reaching them were dropped.
what_to_restore: Five SurrealDatabase repair and SCIP accessors.
InMemoryKb003Storage: un-gated, or replaced by an equivalent the tests can construct.
scope.embedded_mode_boundary: SurrealDB and EventLedger only. Restoring an accessor must not restore any SQLite or PostgreSQL path. If an accessor cannot be restored without reintroducing a removed backend, stop and report it rather than reaching for the old implementation.
acceptance_criteria: AC-149-1: all seven previously failing backend test targets compile. Measure with cargo check --all-targets AND --keep-going: plain cargo check stops scheduling after errors and under-reported this same tree as 2 failing when the truth was 34.

AC-149-2: each restored accessor is reconnected to the SAME durable data it read before. Restoring a name while returning a default, an empty collection, or a stub is a worse outcome than leaving it missing, because the tests would go green while proving nothing.

AC-149-3: the tests in knowledge_code_index_tests that carry MT-108's and MT-105's acceptance proofs execute and pass. Compiling is not sufficient; these are the proofs the whole microtask exists to make executable again.

AC-149-4: No tests/ changes except the two Operator-approved starvation_watermark_at_utc initializers in micro_task_job_tests.rs: Some(now) in the populated literal and None in the optional-none literal. Preserve every assertion. All other test edits require a new Operator decision.
AC-149-5: no accessor is restored by reintroducing SQLite or PostgreSQL.
AC-149-6: the product binary still builds and no unrelated behaviour changes. Restoring visibility should not alter runtime behaviour for anything that already compiled.
proof_targets: PT-149-1: cargo check --all-targets --keep-going before and after, with the failing-target count quoted verbatim both times.
PT-149-2: the knowledge_code_index_tests targets run, not merely compiled, with their result lines quoted.
PT-149-3: for each restored accessor, the evidence that it reads the same durable field it read before b1802e5d - a diff against that commit is the natural source.
execution_constraints: Operator override 2026-09-06: all Cargo targets use ../Handshake/_Artifacts/m149; reuse the existing MT-149 cache, then remove this owned target subfolder after proof and handoff evidence are preserved.

HANDSHAKE_ARTIFACTS_ROOT must resolve to ../Handshake/_Artifacts. Do not create any sibling Handshake_Artifacts folder. Set TEMP and TMP below this root for every proof command; inspect scripts for overrides.
Keep target paths SHORT: bundled DuckDB C++ headers hit the MSVC 260-character limit and fail with C1083.
Cap test concurrency at --test-threads=4. At default parallelism this suite livelocked: 29 tests opened 26 concurrent stores and completed 4 in 3.8 hours.
Serialise linking with -j 1 if you hit LNK1102 out of memory.
Other lanes are live in the same worktree. Stage by explicit path, never git add -A, and never kill a process you did not start.
scope.risk_if_missed: MT-141 stays blocked, the backend suite is never run, and the work packet cannot reach a ready state. Worse, the failure mode this microtask prevents is the tempting one: a future session under time pressure deletes the seven tests, gets a green compile, and silently destroys MT-108's and MT-105's acceptance evidence inside their own packet.

user_manual_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Restores previously-existing accessors; no command, config key, channel or navigation path changes.

risks: Restoring the name but not the wiring - returning a default, an empty vec or a stub so the tests compile and pass while proving nothing. This is the single most likely failure here and AC-149-2 exists for it.
Editing tests/ to meet the accessor halfway, which recreates the exact harm this microtask was created to undo.
Reintroducing a SQLite or PostgreSQL path while restoring an accessor from its pre-pivot implementation.
Declaring success on compilation alone without running the MT-108 and MT-105 proofs.
minimum_controls: AC-149-2 requires each accessor reconnected to the same durable data, with PT-149-3 evidencing it against b1802e5d.
AC-149-3 requires the proofs to run, not just compile.
AC-149-4 forbids touching tests/ and routes any apparent need to the Operator.
AC-149-1 mandates --keep-going so the failing count is not under-reported.

hbr_obligations.INT: Restores previously-existing accessors. If any restoration changes observable runtime behaviour rather than only visibility, that must be recorded under the HBR-INT-009 three-tier consideration.
hbr_obligations.VIS: NOT_APPLICABLE: no GUI, operator, diagnostic or frontend surface.
hbr_obligations.QUIET: Compiles and test runs stay headless.
hbr_obligations.STOP: No capacity or session-count stop reasons. An accessor that cannot be restored without reintroducing a removed backend is reported, not forced.
